title: A payer letter that writes the call's own name with a space or a period anywhere inside a part, whatever the pieces it leaves (`Zephy ra`, `Zephy. ra`, `Z e p h y r a`, an initial beside it), a member ID or claim number with the separator the records themselves hold between two of its characters (`ZZ12345/01`, `ZZ12345.01`, `ZZ12345,01`, `ZZ12345+01`; a claim number held `1234.56` with no label before it), or, with CR LF line endings, a Social Security or phone number that the same letter written with LF is refused for (`SSN on file. Statement`, CR LF and `No. 900-12-3456150.00`)
assertion: Each such name and number is the call's own placeholder in a letter the first reading sends, and a text that still holds one is refused (the check reads what redaction reads; a property over the name's parts, the places they are split and the pieces' case). A letter the first reading's check refuses, as written or with its CR LF line endings as LF, is returned as the first reading wrote it and refused, with the screen and without it (`redactLetter`): no wider placeholder hides what that check read (a claim number held as a held range's amount, a member ID held as a chain's tail). A CR LF letter is refused wherever its writing with LF is (a property), and sent as written where neither writing is refused. The recorded cost is pinned: for a patient whose name's letters are ordinary words apart, those words are replaced and the letter is still sent (`in a` for INA, `is a` for ISA, `as a` for ASA, `to be` for TOBE, `I'd a` for IDA); a claim's digits as a currency amount with cents and a whole written date with no label before it stay; the narrative's check and the packet verifier read as before (`in a` is no name there). The further costs the reviews found are pinned as they are (a letter refused where a label reads through a wider placeholder to a number or the name written apart is glued to a replaced number; a deadline's month, half a hyphenated word or `P.O.` replaced for a patient whose name's letters they are; `$1234.56` for a claim held `1234.56`), and the forms still sent (a part split by a comma, a colon, a parenthesis or another script's full stop; a stored number with another separator). The wider reading, the check asked before a wider match is applied and the check's second reading of a CR LF letter count their work on the letter check's one counter, never a clock (`CHECK_WORK_BUDGET`, MOD-24; docs/adr/0054, amendment of 2026-11-12, item 26's readings on the check's work budget): a letter with such a name is read within the budget, refused by the check where the redaction ended within it and returned as the checks' own mark alone where the redaction passed it, the same answer and count on every run; a CR LF letter is refused at a length its writing with LF is read at; without the screen (`redactLetter`) a letter past the budget is the first reading's text with the mark after it and never sent as the first reading alone wrote it (which the check by itself could send with `tree` of `Van tree` in clear for a patient VAN VANTREE), with nothing the first reading redacts shown; a letter the first reading refuses is refused within the budget and past it; a letter with nothing for the wider reading to apply costs the redaction what it cost before. A letter that holds such a name once among dates or thousands of times, a CR LF letter with no such name, and a CR LF letter with one, at lengths still read (25,000 to 100,000 characters), are each redacted and checked within the budget of 3 seconds of the reader's own processor time on the reference machine (`test-support/time-budget.ts`); the same letters at 100,000 characters, and review C's letters of one digit to a line with a name written apart or one CR LF (3.0 to 3.8 s before), are refused by the count well within it; and a letter with no invisible run is still read once (the regular-expression run count)
noFileReason: Letters are written in memory by the tests, two properties among them; no file.
